ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Accord of Difference and Sameness is the title of Shitou Xiqian’s verse, identified as a composed work, quoted by its opening and closing lines, and discussed by later masters.
EvidenceBody: The title combines participation or joining , sameness , and accord or tally . In the Chan corpus it is the proper name of Shitou Xiqian's verse. The Transmission of the Lamp says that Shitou wrote it, calls its language deep, and prints the work under his name. Its opening says that the mind of the great Indian immortal is intimately transmitted east and west ; its closing tells the person investigating the mystery to meet the source on hearing words and not waste the daylight . Fayan Wenyi later invokes the title in hall discourse, calls it a piece of wording, and quotes its opening. The Joint Essentials of the Lamps connects Shitou's composition with his reading that the sage has no self and nothing is not himself . Zen bends the phrase into a lineage-specific bibliographic name: these records use it not for a general agreement but for Shitou's transmitted Chan poem and for quotations from that poem.
